verdict.rationale: OpenCode documents a plan agent that analyzes code and reviews suggestions without modifying files. Its permission system can prompt before actions run, and its GitHub integration works on a branch and opens a PR, which gives a pre-merge review point. However, the evidence never documents a built-in diff viewer or running tests, linters, or checks before merging. missing for 10: explicit diff inspection UI/command, documented ability to run tests/lint/checks as a pre-merge gate, independent hands-on corroboration of a review workflow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can inspect diffs and run checks to catch problems before merging

citations.quote: Use the plan agent to analyze code and review suggestions without making any code changes.
This agent is useful when you want the LLM to analyze code, suggest changes, or create plans without making any actual modifications to your codebase.
OpenCode uses the `permission` config to decide whether a given action should run automatically, prompt you, or be blocked.
it will work in a new branch and submits a PR with all the changes.
